MATH 101.name: Calculus I
MATH 101.description: Limits and continuity. Differentiation and applications (linearization, optimization, curve sketching, l'Hôpital's rule). Integration and applications (areas, volumes, arc lengths, surface areas). Transcendental functions. Integration techniques. Improper integrals.

MATH 102.name: Calculus II
MATH 102.description: Sequences and series, power series, Taylor series. Functions of several variables: partial derivatives and gradient, free and constrained extrema, multiple integrals, Fubini's theorems. Line integrals, Green's theorem. Surface integrals, Divergence theorem, Stokes' theorem.

MATH 103.name: Thinking Mathematically I
MATH 103.description: Critical thinking and problem solving. Set theory. Logic; inductive and deductive reasoning. The real number system, integers, rational and irrational numbers. Exponents and scientific notation, roots. Algebraic equations and inequalities. Linear and quadratic equations. Functions and graphs; graph reading. Exponential, logarithmic, and quadratic functions.

MATH 104.name: Thinking Mathematically II
MATH 104.description: Consumer mathematics, simple and compound interest annuities and bonds. Measurement and unit conversion. Plane geometry; areas and volumes. Counting, permutations and combinations. Fundamentals of probability. Descriptive statistics. Voting and apportionment. Elementary graph theory.

MATH 105.name: Introduction to Calculus I
MATH 105.description: Inequalities, absolute value. Cartesian plane, graphs of equations (lines, circles and parabolas). Functions, functions in economics, trigonometric functions. Limits, continuity. Derivative, differentiation rules, chain rule, implicit differentiation, marginal functions in economics. Maximum and minimum values, increasing and decreasing functions, the first derivative test, concavity, the second derivative test, curve sketching using calculus, optimization problems and applications in business and economics.

MATH 106.name: Introduction to Calculus II
MATH 106.description: Indefinite integral, definite integral, fundamental theorem of calculus, method of substitution, area between two curves. Inverse functions and their derivatives, exponential and logarithmic functions, inverse trigonometric functions. Indeterminate forms and l'Hôpital's Rule. Geometric series, compound interest, exponential growth and decay. Techniques of integration (integration by parts, rationalizing substitution, partial fractions), improper integrals. Differential equations (separable and first-order linear equations) and initial-value problems. Three-dimensional coordinate system, functions of several variables, partial derivatives, the chain rule. Maximum and minimum values, the second partials test, the method of Lagrange Multipliers. Double integrals.

MATH 110.name: Discrete Mathematics
MATH 110.description: Sets and propositions: Finite and infinite sets, mathematical induction, propositions. Permutations, combinations, and discrete probability. Relations and functions: binary, equivalence relations, partitions, partial ordering, functions. Graphs: weighted graphs, paths and circuits, shortest paths. Eulerian and Hamiltonian paths. Trees. Abstract algebra: groups, cosets, Lagrange's theorem, Boolean algebra.

MATH 123.name: Abstract Mathematics I
MATH 123.description: Fundamental principles of counting, mathematical logic, basic set theory, the principle of mathematical induction and its variations, relations and functions, enumeration of relations and functions, equinumerous, finite, denumerable, uncountable sets, Cantor-Bernstein Theorem, Axiom of Choice, Zorn’s Lemma, cardinal numbers.

MATH 124.name: Abstract Mathematics II
MATH 124.description: Natural numbers, rational numbers, sequences, construction of real numbers, principles of inclusion-exclusion, generating functions, recurrence relations, groups, homomorphisms, isomorphisms, cyclic groups, cosets, Lagrange's Theorem, Burnside's Theorem, permutation groups, cycle structure, Polya's method of enumeration, basics of graphs, trees, counting unlabeled graphs.

MATH 132.name: Discrete and Combinatorial Mathematics
MATH 132.description: Fundamental principles of counting, including rules of sums and product, permutations and combinations. Fundamentals of logic and integers, including mathematical induction, recursive definitions, prime numbers, greatest common divisor, Cartesian products and relations, pigeonhole principle, partial orders, equivalence relations and partitions. The principle of inclusion and exclusion. Sums and recurrence relations: first and second order linear recurrence relations, finite and infinite calculus, infinite sums. Integer functions including floor and ceiling applications and recurrences, and the modulo operation. Generating functions including the method of generating functions for solving recurrences and exponential generating functions. Introduction to graph theory including graph isomorphism, Euler tours, Hamiltonian paths and cycles, planar graphs, and graph coloring.

MATH 202.name: Complex Analysis
MATH 202.description: Algebra of complex numbers, topology of the complex plane. Analytic functions, Cauchy-Riemann equations, power series. Complex line integrals, Cauchy theorem, Cauchy integral formula, Taylor series. Mean value property, Liouville theorem, isolated zeros, uniqueness theorem, maximum modulus principle. Isolated singularities, singularities at infinity, Laurent series. Residues, evaluation of improper integrals.

MATH 210.name: Finite and Discrete Mathematics
MATH 210.description: Sets and propositions. Mathematical induction. Recurrence relations. Graph theory: trees, Euler paths, planar graphs, graph isomorphism. Enumerative combinatorics: binomial coefficients, pigeonhole principle, relations and incidence matrices, functions, isomorphism of posets, Hasse diagrams, equivalence relations, Stirling numbers of the second kind.

MATH 213.name: Introduction to Real Analysis I
MATH 213.description: The real number system, least upper bound property. Sequences in R, Cauchy sequences, limsup and liminf. Limit and continuity in R, uniform continuity. Differentiation in R. Riemann integral in R, fundamental theorem of calculus. Infinite series of numbers, absolute convergence. Sequences and series of functions, uniform convergence, power series.

MATH 214.name: Introduction to Real Analysis II
MATH 214.description: Euclidean spaces, topology of Rn. Differentiability on Rn , differentials, inverse and implicit function theorems. Riemann integral on Rn, Jordan regions, change of variables. Vector calculus, curves and surfaces, Green, Gauss, Stokes theorems.

MATH 215.name: Mathematical Analysis
MATH 215.description: The real number system. The complex field. Finite, countable, uncountable sets. Metric spaces. Compact sets, connected sets. Sequences, Cauchy sequences. Series of numbers, summation by parts. Continuity, uniform continuity. Continuity and compactness, continuity and connectedness. Sequences and series of functions. Uniform convergence and continuity/integration/differentiation.
MATH 215.prerequisite: MATH 102 or MATH 106 or MATH 114 or MATH 116

MATH 220.name: Linear Algebra
MATH 220.description: Introduction to matrices. Fields and vector spaces, linear transformations, change of basis. Linear equations, existence and classification of solutions, Gaussian elimination and LU decomposition. Characteristic equation of a matrix: eigenvalues, eigenvectors and the Jordan form. Numerical techniques for computing eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Inner product spaces, quadratic forms.

MATH 223.name: Abstract Linear Algebra
MATH 223.description: Vector spaces, subspaces, linear combinations and systems of linear equations, Linear Dependence and Linear Independence, bases and dimension, Linear transformations and matrices, Null Spaces, and Ranges, Matrix Representation of a Linear Transformation, Composition of Linear Transformations, Invertibility and Isomorphisms, Change of Coordinate Matrix, Elementary Matrix Operations, Rank, Determinants and its properties, Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors, Diagonalizability, Inner Products, Gram Schmidt, Orthogonal Complements.

MATH 225.name: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
MATH 225.description: Systems of linear equations, Elimination methods, matrices and matrix operations. Invertible matrices, determinants. Vector spaces, basis and dimension. Inner product spaces, orthogonality, orthogonal basis, rank and nullity. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors, systems of differential equations, matrix-valued functions. First and second order linear differential equations. n-th order linear differential equations, method of undetermined coefficient, variation of parameters.

MATH 227.name: Introduction to Linear Algebra
MATH 227.description: Introduction to matrices, basic definitions and properties. Linear equations; inverse and rank of a matrix; existence and classification of solutions; Gaussian elimination. Characteristic equation of a matrix; eigenvalues, eigenvectors. Numerical techniques. Applications.

MATH 230.name: Probability and Statistics for Engineers
MATH 230.description: Basic concepts of probability (sample spaces and events, permutations, combinations, conditional probability and independence). Discrete and continuous random variables, their probability distributions, expected value and distribution parameters. Discrete probability distributions: Binomial, geometric, negative binomial, Poisson distributions. Continuous probability distributions: uniform, normal, exponential, gamma and chi-squared distributions. Jointly distributed and independent Random Variables. Covariance and correlation. The sampling distribution of sample mean. Central Limit Theorem and its applications. Estimation. Confidence Intervals, Hypothesis Testing.

MATH 240.name: Differential Equations
MATH 240.description: First and second order differential equations, existence and uniqueness of solutions. Linear homogeneous differential equations. Linear nonhomogeneous equations: the methods of undetermined coefficients and variation of parameters, reduction of order. Series solution of second order equations. Systems of first order differential equations. Solution by Laplace transforms. Numerical solution techniques.

MATH 241.name: Engineering Mathematics I
MATH 241.description: Introduction to complex algebra. Systems of linear equations, Gaussian elimination. Vector spaces and their extension to complex case, linear dependence/independence, bases. Matrix algebra, determinant, inverse, factorization. Eigenvalue problem, diagonalization, quadratic forms. Linear approximation, curve fitting. Linear constant coefficient difference equations and the z-transform. Linear constant coefficient differential equations and the Laplace transform. System of linear differential equations.

MATH 242.name: Engineering Mathematics II
MATH 242.description: Differential equations of first order, separable equations. Linear differential equations of higher order, homogeneous and nonhomogeneous equations. Numerical solutions of differential equations. Runge-Kutta method, boundary-value problems. Differential calculus of functions of several variables, Taylor series approximation. Jacobians, maxima and minima of a function, Method of Lagrange multipliers. Functions of a complex variable, differential complex calculus. Complex integration, Cauchy's theorem. Complex series, Taylor and Laurent series. Residue theorem.

MATH 250.name: Introduction to Probability
MATH 250.description: Basic concepts of probability, conditional probability. Random variables, expectation and variance. Binomial, geometric, negative binomial, hypergeometric, Poisson random variables. Moment generating functions. Continous random variables: Uniform, Exponential, Gamma, Normal, Beta, Weibull distributions. Bivariate and marginal distributions. Conditional distributions, covariance and correlation coefficient, conditional expectations.

MATH 253.name: Introduction to Number Theory
MATH 253.description: Divisibility, congruences, quadratic reciprocity, arithmetical functions, irrational numbers, simple continued fractions, Diophantine equations.

MATH 255.name: Probability and Statistics
MATH 255.description: Basic concepts of probability, expectation and variance, distribution functions, Bayes' formula, marginal and conditional distributions, the distributions of sample statistics, law of large numbers, central limit theorem, introduction to hypothesis testing.

MATH 260.name: Introduction to Statistics
MATH 260.description: Descriptive statistics, sampling and sampling distributions. Introduction to estimation theory, method of maximum likelihood and method of moments, interval estimation. Tests of hypotheses, two population problems, correlation. Simple linear regression analysis, nonlinear regression. Multiple regression analysis.

MATH 262.name: Statistical Methodology
MATH 262.description: Organization and description of data. Basic concepts of probability. Binomial, Poisson distributions. The normal distribution. X2, t and F distributions. Simple and multiple regression. Analysis of categorical data. Some nonparametric tests. Biological and medical science applications using a statistical software such as MINITAB or SAS.

MATH 264.name: Statistics for Social Sciences
MATH 264.description: Introduction to statistics with special emphasis on the utilization of statistical methods in social sciences: Organization of data, measures of center and variability. Basic probability concepts. Discrete and continuous random variables and their distributions. Inferences about the mean. Applications using statistical computer programs.

MATH 291.name: Summer Project I
MATH 291.description: A project on a specific topic in an area of mathematics to be carried out by the students under the supervision of a faculty member.

MATH 300.name: A Concise History of Mathematics
MATH 300.description: The emergence and development of mathematical ideas and techniques during the last few millennia starting with the early Egyptian papyri and ending with the twentieth century mathematics. Tracing the philosophical and cultural setting of mathematics through some concrete problems which include the unit fractions, perfect numbers, Diophantine equations, ruler and compass constructions, polynomial roots, limits, infinity and some unsolved problems of elementary mathematics.

MATH 302.name: Complex Analysis II
MATH 302.description: Evaluation of sums by residues. Argument principle, Rouche theorem, open mapping theorem. Conformal mapping, mapping by elementary functions. Riemann sphere, linear fractional transformations. Schwarz lemma, automorphisms of the disc and the upper half plane. Schwarz-Christoffel transformations. Applications to fluid flow and electrostatics. Harmonic functions, Poisson integral formula. Infinite products, entire and meromorphic functions, gamma and zeta functions.

MATH 310.name: Topology
MATH 310.description: Topological spaces, connected and compact spaces, continuous functions, product spaces, the Tychonoff theorem, separation axioms, separation by continuous functions, complete metric spaces, applications. Fundamental group and covering spaces: homotopy, fundamental group, covering spaces.

MATH 313.name: Metric Spaces
MATH 313.description: Metric spaces, sequences, completeness, Baire's theorem. Continuity. Completion of a metric space. Compactness and connectedness. Contraction mapping theorem and its applications. Product spaces.

MATH 314.name: Measure Theory
MATH 314.description: Lebesgue outer measure, measurable sets. Lebesgue integral, convergence theorems. Functions of bounded variation, absolutely continuous functions. Lp spaces. General measure and integration theory. Radon-Nikodym theorem. Product measures, Fubini's theorem.

MATH 315.name: Fourier Analysis
MATH 315.description: Inner product spaces, approximation in the mean, complete orthonormal systems. Fourier series, pointwise and uniform convergence, Gibbs phenomenon, applications to PDE. Fourier transform, Fourier inversion, Plancherel identity. Applications; heat kernel, sampling theorem, uncertainty principle. Discrete Fourier transforms.
MATH 315.prerequisite: (MATH 102 or MATH 106) and (MATH 220 or MATH 223 or MATH 241)

MATH 316.name: Orthogonal Functions
MATH 316.description: Linear spaces. Finite-dimensional linear spaces. Infinite-dimensional linear spaces. Inner products. Orthogonal functions and vectors. Orthogonal sequences. Differential operators. Integral operators. Convolution. Fourier series. Sine and cosine series. The Gibbs phenomenon. Local convergence of Fourier series. Divergent series. Generalized functions. Legendre polynomials.
MATH 316.prerequisite: (MATH 102 or MATH 106) and (MATH 220 or MATH 223 or MATH 241)

MATH 319.name: Interpolation and Approximation
MATH 319.description: Chebyshev polynominals. Polynominal interpolation. Divided differences. Lebesgue constants. Hermite interpolation and Birkhoff interpolation. Bernstein polynominals. Uniform approximation of functions. Characterization of the best approximation. Uniqueness of the best approximation, Haar systems. Fekete points, Leja sequence and approximation of the Green function. Polynomial inequalities. Some extremal problems. Degree of approximation. Jackson and Bernstein theorems. Interpolation and approximation by splines.
MATH 319.prerequisite: (MATH 102 or MATH 106) and (MATH 220 or MATH 223 or MATH 241)

MATH 323.name: Algebra I: Groups
MATH 323.description: Groups, dihedral groups, symmetric groups, quaternion groups, homomorphisms, isomorphisms, group actions, subgroups, centralizers, normalizers, stabilizers, kernels, cyclic groups, lattices, quotient groups, cosets, Lagrange's theorem, isomorphism theorems, composition series, Alternating groups, permutation representations, Cayley’s theorem, the class equation, automorphisms, Sylow theorems, simplicity of alternating group, direct products, finitely generated abelian groups, small order groups, semidirect products, nilpotent groups, solvable groups, p-groups, medium order groups, free groups.

MATH 324.name: Algebra II
MATH 324.description: Symmetries of polynomial equations. Rings and modules. Quotient rings and polynomial rings. Field Extensions. Ruler-and-compass constructions. Euclidean domains, principal ideal domains, unique factorization domains. Finitely generated modules of principal ideal domains. Eisenstein's Criterion. Galois groups. The Fundamental Theorem of Galois Theory. The Unsolvability of the Quintic.

MATH 325.name: Representation Theory
MATH 325.description: Module theory, semisimple rings and modules, Artin-Wedderburn theorem. Characters, orthonormality properties of character tables. Induction, restriction and inflation of characters. Calculating character tables. Burnsides' solubility theorem, Frobenius' normal complement theorem.
MATH 325.prerequisite: MATH 323 and (MATH 220 or MATH 223 or MATH 225 or MATH 241)

MATH 327.name: Algebra II: Rings and Modules
MATH 327.description: Rings, Polynomial Rings, Matrix Rings, Group Rings, Ring Homomorphism, Quotient Rings, Ideals, Ring of Fractions, the Chinese Remainder Theorem, Euclidean Domains, Principal Ideal Domains, Unique Factorization Domains, Irreducibility Criteria, Göbner Basis, Modules, Quotient Modules, Module Homomorphisms, Generation of Modules, Direct Sums, Free Module, Tensor Product, Exact Sequences, Projective, Injective, and Flat Modules, Vector Spaces, Linear Transformation Matrices, Dual Vector Spaces, Determinants, Tensor Algebras, Symmetric and Exterior Algebras, Modules over Principal Ideal Domains, Rational Canonical Form, Jordan Canonical Form.

MATH 328.name: Algebra III: Field and Galois Theory
MATH 328.description: Field Extensions, Algebraic Extensions, Classical Straightedge and Compass Constructions, Splitting Fields, Algebraic Closure, Separable and Inseparable Extensions, Cyclotomic Polynomials and Extensions, Galois Theory, the Fundamental Theorem of Galois Theory, Finite Fields, Composite Extensions, Simple Extensions, Abelian Extensions over Rationals, Galois Groups of Polynomials, Solvable and Radical Extensions, Insolvability of the Quintic, Computation of Galois Groups over Rationals, Transcendental Extensions, Infinite Galois Groups, Noetherian Rings, Affine Varieties, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, Localization, the Prime Spectrum of a Ring, Artinian Rings, Discrete Valuation Rings, and Dedekind Domains.

MATH 330.name: Principles of Applied Mathematics
MATH 330.description: Fundamental ideas of applied mathematics. Modeling approaches, deterministic and stochastic models. Transformation and approximation methods. Dimensional analysis, similarity solutions, perturbation methods and asymptotic expansions. ODE and PDE models, reaction-diffusion equations, pattern formation, wave phenomena. Variational principles. Applications to physical and biological sciences.

MATH 340.name: Mathematical Foundations of Statistical Mechanics
MATH 340.description: System of Statistical Mechanics, Statistical Ensembles. Random fields, Product measures, finite and infinite volume Gibbs Distributions. Markov property. Probabilistic methods: Borel-Cantelly lemma and Kolmogorov type 0-1 laws. Phase transitions. ferromagnetical and antiferromagnetical Ising model. Pierls inequality. Correlation functions and Griffith inequalities. Thermodynamic limit. Transfer matrix. Cluster expansions.

MATH 344.name: Introduction to Dynamical Systems
MATH 344.description: Systems oflinear differential equations, phase portraits. Nonlinear equations. Existence and uniqueness theorems. Flows and limit sets. Equilibrium and periodic solutions. Local stability and the linearization principle. Global stability and the Liapunov method. Planar systems and the Poincaré-Bendixson theorem. Invariant manifolds. Bifurcations. Discrete dynamical systems. Strange attractors and chaos. Numerical methods. Applications in biology, mechanics, and engineering.

MATH 345.name: Differential Geometry I
MATH 345.description: Euclidean spaces and differential forms, frames, calculus on surfaces. Shape operators. Gaussian and mean curvatures.
MATH 345.prerequisite: (MATH 102 or MATH 106) and (MATH 220 or MATH 223 or MATH 225 or MATH 241)

MATH 346.name: Differential Geometry II
MATH 346.description: Intrinsic geometry of surfaces. Riemannian geometry. Geodesics. Gauss-Bonnet theorem. Global structure of surfaces.

MATH 391.name: Summer Project II
MATH 391.description: A project on a specific topic in an area of mathematics to be carried out by the students under the supervision of a faculty member.

MATH 399.name: Summer Practice
MATH 399.description: The minimum time for this practice is 4 weeks (20 working days). The main objective is to gain practical work experience in an academic/governmental/private institution in areas related to mathematics.

MATH 414.name: Functional Analysis
MATH 414.description: Normed spaces. Compactness in Banach spaces. Linear operators. Dual spaces, reflexivity. Hilbert spaces. Orthogonal sequences in Hilbert spaces. Operators in Hilbert spaces. Hahn-Banach theorem. Uniform boundedness principle. Open mapping and closed graph theorems. Weak and weak* convergence.

MATH 415.name: Analysis of Differentiable Functions
MATH 415.description: Algebra of smooth functions. Faa di Bruno formula. Critical values. Sard theorem. Real analytic functions. Pringsheim-Boas criterion. Extension of differentiable functions. Whitney functions. Partition of unity. Polynomial interpolation. Lebesgue constants. Approximation by polynomials, smooth and analytic functions. Elements of harmonic analysis.

MATH 420.name: Introduction to Cryptography
MATH 420.description: This course is designed as an introduction to public key cryptology. We will review the mathematical background material as needed but rather than giving rigorous proofs of the theorems we emphasize their computational aspects by presenting algorithms and their implementations . Topics include Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange, Standard and Elliptic ElGamal Public Key Cryptosystem, RSA Public Key Cryptosystem, The Knapsack Cryptosystem, Digital Signatures and Hash Functions.

MATH 421.name: Introduction to Quantum Computation
MATH 421.description: Axioms of quantum mechanics. Density operators. Quantum teleportation, superdense coding. Bell inequalities. Models for computation and computational complexity. Quantum circuits: single qubit operations, controlled operations. Universality of quantum gates. Deutsch's algorithm, Shor's algorithm, Grover's algorithm.
MATH 421.prerequisite: MATH 220 or MATH 223 or MATH 225 or MATH 241

MATH 422.name: Topics in Quantum Information Theory
MATH 422.description: Selected topics in quantum information theory. Quantum operations, distance measures for quantum states and channels. Quantum error-correction: Shor code, Calderbarnk-Shor-Steane codes and stabilizer codes. Quantum entropy and its properties. Information-theoretic protocols: quantum data compression and noisy quantum channels. Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution, BB84 protocol and its security proof.
MATH 422.prerequisite: MATH 220 or MATH 223 or MATH 225 or MATH 241

MATH 424.name: Advanced Linear Algebra
MATH 424.description: Determinant Functions, Multilinear Functions, The Grassman Ring, Characteristic values, annihilating polynomials, invariant subspaces, simultaneous triangulation, simultaneous diagonalization, direct-sum decompositions, invariant direct sums, primary decomposition theorem, cyclic subspaces, annihilators, rational canonical form, Jordan form, invariant factors, semisimple operators, inner products, inner product spaces, linear functionals, adjoints, unitary operators, normal operators, bilinear forms, sesquilinear forms, positive forms, spectral theory, symmetric bilinear forms, skew-symmetric forms, groups preserving bilinear forms.

MATH 429.name: Finite Group Theory
MATH 429.description: Group actions, p-groups, Sylow theorems, the Frattini argument, characterizations of nilpotent groups, the Fitting subgroup, the Chermak-Delgado measure, subnormality, Brodkey's theorem, split extensions, the Schur-Zassenhaus theorem, Hall theorems, Carter subgroups, coprime actions, Glauberman's lemma, commutator identities, nilpotence classes, Thompson's P x Q lemma, Baer's trick, transfer homomorphisms, focal subgroups, Frobenius p-nilpotency theorems, the Burnside fusion theorem, resistant p-groups, Frobenius groups, and fixed-point-free automorphisms.

MATH 430.name: Introduction to Complex Geometry
MATH 430.description: Vector bundles. Sheaf theory and sheaf cohomology. Kahler manifolds. Chow rings. Lefschetz (1,1)-theorem. The Hodge conjecture, i.e. the (p,p) version of Lefschetz's theorem.

MATH 431.name: Introduction to Algebraic Geometry
MATH 431.description: Plane curves, conics and cubics. Affine varieties, Hilbert basis theorem, Zarisky topology, Hibert's null stellennsatz. Coordinate rings, morphisms. Projective varieties, briational morphism. Smoothness, dimension and the tangent space. The 27 lines on a cubic surface.

MATH 440.name: Dynamical Systems
MATH 440.description: Geometric theory of differential equations. Existence and uniqueness theorems; continuous dependence on initial conditions and parameters. Flows for autonomous and non-autonomous systems. Topological conjugacy and equivalence, Hartman-Grobman theorem. Stability theory. Non-autonomous linear systems and Floquet theory. Periodic solutions and Poincaré maps. Global methods, Liapunov theory and LaSalle invariance principle. Stable, unstable, and center manifolds. Structural stability and bifurcation theory. Symbolic dynamics and the shift map. Homoclinic phenomena.

MATH 443.name: Partial Differential Equations
MATH 443.description: Pfaffian systems, linear and nonlinear PDE's of first order. Second order PDE, characteristic curves and characteristic equations. Laplace equation, wave equation, heat equation. Method of integral transforms, Fourier series, Green's function.

MATH 445.name: Analysis on Manifolds
MATH 445.description: The algebra and topology of Rn, review of differentiation and integration, inverse and implicit function theorems change of variables, tensors and differential forms, integration on chains, integration on manifolds, and Stokes' theorem.
MATH 445.prerequisite: (MATH 102 or MATH 106) and (MATH 220 or MATH 223 or MATH 241)

MATH 450.name: Probability Theory
MATH 450.description: Sample spaces, sigma algebras, probability measures, measurable sets and functions, random variables, independence, Borel-Cantelli Lemmas, expectation, Monotone convergence theorem, Fatou's lemma, dominated convergence theorem, modes of convergence, weak and strong law of large numbers, moment-generating and characteristic functions, Central Limit Theorem (CLT), Lindeberg-Feller CLT, conditional expectations, Martingales and Martingale Convergence Theorem.
MATH 450.prerequisite: MATH 213 and (MATH 230 or MATH 250 or MATH 255)

MATH 453.name: Algebraic Number Theory
MATH 453.description: Principal ideal domains, unique factorization domains, residue classes. Algebraic integers. Integral basis. Discriminant. Quadratic and cyclotomic extensions. Norm and trace. Ideals. Bounds for the discriminant. Units. Dirichlet's problem. Ramification of prime ideals.

MATH 460.name: Theory of Statistics
MATH 460.description: Review of probability, decision problems and loss functions, methods of point estimation: maximum likelihood and moment method, unbiasedness, consistency, sufficiency, Neyman-Fisher factorization theorem, Complete statistics. Lehmann-Scheffétheorem, Rao-Blackwell theorem. Fisher information and its properties. Cramer-Rao lower bound, Efficiency of estimators. Confidence Intervals: Theory and Construction, Hypothesis testing and Neyman-Pearson Lemma, Uniformly Most Powerful (UMP) and Likelihood Ratio Tests, Bayesian hypothesis testing. Asymptotic Methods in Estimation and Testing.

MATH 465.name: Mathematical Foundations of Data Science
MATH 465.description: Review of eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Fundamental subspaces, matrix factorization techniques, principal components and best low-rank matrices; the structure of neural nets for deep learning. Convergence concepts and limit theorems in probability, basic inequalities of probability, tail bounds, the concentration of measures phenomena, empirical process. Maximum likelihood estimation, regularized regression, the Lasso and its variations. Optimization methods, gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, convolutional neural nets.
MATH 465.prerequisite: (MATH 230 or MATH 250 or MATH 255) and (MATH 220 or MATH 223 or MATH 225 or MATH 241)

MATH 473.name: Introduction to Financial Mathematics
MATH 473.description: Basic knowledge and techniques in financial mathematics: basic Black and Scholes model and its sophistications. Theory of discrete and continuous martingales, semimartingales. Stochastic integral, Ito formula, construction and solution of stochastic differential equations. Applications to option pricing and hedging problems for the European options. American options and the numerical problems of the solutions of second order elliptic equations.

MATH 474.name: Financial Mathematics
MATH 474.description: Calculations practiced in option marketing. Fundamentals of Ito Calculus, and its applications to calculations.

MATH 490.name: Project in Mathematics
MATH 490.description: Independent project synthesizing and complementing regular curriculum material. Making project proposals and designing workflows for investigating topics in the areas of mathematical modelling of real life problems, history of outstanding results and/or mathematicians, scientific software based on mathematical results, and remarkable results from articles and monographs. Written and oral communication of mathematics. Fundamentals of mathematical typesetting with LaTeX. Plagiarism and ethical issues. Exploring mathematical resources.

MATH 491.name: Senior Project I
MATH 491.description: A project on a specific topic in an area of mathematics to be carried out by the students under the supervision of a faculty member.

MATH 492.name: Senior Project II
MATH 492.description: A project on a specific topic in an area of mathematics to be carried out by the students under the supervision of a faculty member.

MATH 500.name: Mathematical Analysis
MATH 500.description: Metric spaces, sequences, completeness, Baire's theorem. Continuity. Completion of a metric space. Compactness and connectedness. Contraction mapping theorem and its applications. Product spaces.

MATH 501.name: Real Analysis I
MATH 501.description: Concepts of integration. Generalized Riemann Integral. Borel Sets, Bair Functions. Outer Measures. Measurable Sets. Lebesgue Measure. Lebesgue density theorem. Hausdorff Dimension. Measurable Functions. Lusin's and Egorov's Theorems. Limit Theorems for Lebesgue Integral. Differentiation of Lebesgue Integral. Spaces of Integrable Functions. Signed Measures. The Radon-Nikodym Theorem.

MATH 502.name: Real Analysis II
MATH 502.description: Topological vector spaces. Metrizability. Locally convex spaces. Boundedness and normability. Barreled spaces. Banach-Steinhaus theorem. Dual pairs and polar topologies. Topologies on spaces of linear mappings. Inductive and projective limits. Distributions. Elements of spectral theory.

MATH 503.name: Complex Analysis I
MATH 503.description: Complex differentiability and Cauchy-Riemann equations. Holomorphic functions and primitives. Local Cauchy theorems, Morera theorem, power series representations, and fundamental properties of holomorphic functions. Logarithms, winding numbers, and global Cauchy theorems. Singularities, Laurent series, and residue theorem. Argument principle and open mapping theorem. Conformal mapping, Schwarz-Pick lemma, and Mobius transformations. Normal families and Riemann mapping theorem. Harmonic and subharmonic functions, Poisson integrals, and Schwarz reflection principle. Simply connected plane domains.

MATH 504.name: Complex Analysis II
MATH 504.description: Runge theorem and Mittag-Leffler theorem. Infinite products and Weierstrass factorization theorem. Jensen formula and Blaschke products. Special functions. Caratheodory and Lindelof theorems. Analytic continuation, gap series, and monodromy theorem. Cauchy-Pompeiu formula and inhomogeneous d-bar equation. Spaces of holomorphic functions.

MATH 505.name: Introduction to Complex Geometry
MATH 505.description: Vector bundles. Sheaf theory and sheaf cohomology. Kahler manifolds. Chow rings. Lefschetz (1,1)-theorem. The Hodge conjecture, i.e. the (p,p) version of Lefschetz's theorem.

MATH 507.name: Introduction to Potential Theory
MATH 507.description: Harmonic and subharmonic functions. Potentials and Energies. Equilibrim measures. Green functions. Capacities. Exceptional sets. Transfinite diameters and Chebyshev constants. Applications to Approximation Theory.

MATH 509.name: Topics in Operator Theory
MATH 509.description: Spectral theory of linear operators in normed linear spaces. Banach algebras. Spectral theory of compact operators. Bounded selfadjoint operators. Unbounded selfadjoint operators. Unbounded linear operators in quantum mechanics.

MATH 518.name: Topics in Graph Theory
MATH 518.description: Selected topics in graph theory, dealing with undirected, directed, weighted, signed graphs, infinite graphs, and simplicial complexes. Groups and matrices. Random graphs and networks. Algebraic graph theory. Graph spectra. Random walks and dynamics on graphs. Applications.

MATH 521.name: Introduction to Quantum Computation
MATH 521.description: Axioms of quantum mechanics. Density operators. Quantum teleportation, superdense coding. Bell inequalities. Models for computation and computational complexity. Quantum circuits: single qubit operations, controlled operations. Universality of quantum gates. Deutsch's algorithm, Shor's algorithm, Grover's algorithm.

MATH 522.name: Topics in Quantum Information Theory
MATH 522.description: Selected topics in quantum information theory. Quantum operations, distance measures for quantum states and channels. Quantum error-correction: Shor code, Calderbarnk-Shor-Steane codes and stabilizer codes. Quantum entropy and its properties. Information-theoretic protocols: quantum data compression and noisy quantum channels. Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution, BB84 protocol and its security proof.

MATH 523.name: Algebra I
MATH 523.description: Category-theoretic language. Review of groups, rings, modules. Applications of Zorn's Lemma, including the algebraic closure of a field. Galois theory.

MATH 524.name: Algebra II
MATH 524.description: Rings, modules and endomorphism rings. Idempotents and indecomposable modules. Jacobson radical. Artinian and Noetherian rings. Artin-Wedderburn Theorem. Levitsky's Theorem. Krull-Schmidt Theorem. Maschke's Theorem and finite group representations.

MATH 525.name: Representation Theory
MATH 525.description: Representation as linear action. Existence of invariant metric. Maschke theorem. Schur's lemma. Multiplicity of irreducible component in regular representation. Structure of group algebra. Characters and presentations of abelian groups, duality. Characters of non-abelian groups. Central idempotent and the first orthogonality relation. Completeness of the set of characters and the second orthogonality relation. Induced representations and characters. Mackey criterion of irreducibility. Representations of symmetric group. Representations of supersolvable groups. Real representations and Schur's index. Other applications of induced representations. Degrees of irreducible representations. Compact groups, Haar measure. Linear representations of compact groups. Unitary trick. Representations of general linear and unitary groups.

MATH 527.name: Topics in Representation Theory
MATH 527.description: Semisimple rings. Artinian rings. Krull_Schmidt Theorem. Brauer characters. Green Correspondence. Blocks and defect groups. Interior G-algebras, defect groups and source algebras.

MATH 529.name: Finite Group Theory
MATH 529.description: Group actions, p-groups, Sylow theorems, the Frattini argument, characterizations of nilpotent groups, the Fitting subgroup, the Chermak-Delgado measure, subnormality, Brodkey's theorem, split extensions, the Schur-Zassenhaus theorem, Hall theorems, Carter subgroups, coprime actions, Glauberman's lemma, commutator identities, nilpotence classes, Thompson's P × Q lemma, Baer's trick, transfer homomorphisms, focal subgroups, Frobenius p-nilpotency theorems, the Burnside fusion theorem, resistant p-groups, Frobenius groups, and fixed-point-free automorphisms.

MATH 535.name: Topology of Algebraic Varieties
MATH 535.description: Introduction: algebraic varieties, rigidity vs. flexibility, algebro-geometric vs. topological properties. Deformation invariance of topology. Singular vs. nonsingular and real vs. complex varieties. Simple case: Riemann surfaces. Genus, Riemann-Hurwitz formula, topological nature of discrete invariants. A brief introduction to singularities of curves and surfaces. Blow-ups and resolution of singularities. Singular plane curves. Components of the moduli space. The fundamental group. Introduction to Hodge theory (if needed). K3-surfaces: the global Torelli theorem, period spaces, curves and linear systems, topological classification (including singular, symmetric, and real surfaces). Polarized K3-surfaces: plane sextics and quartics in space. Hyperelliptic and trigonal curves in Hirzebruch surfaces; elliptic surfaces.

MATH 540.name: Dynamical Systems
MATH 540.description: Geometric theory of differential equations. Existence and uniqueness theorems; continuous dependence on initial conditions and parameters. Flows for autonomous and non-autonomous systems. Topological conjugacy and equivalence, Hartman-Grobman theorem. Stability theory. Non-autonomous linear systems and Floquet theory. Periodic solutions and Poincaré maps. Global methods, Liapunov theory and LaSalle invariance principle. Stable, unstable, and center manifolds. Structural stability and bifurcation theory. Symbolic dynamics and the shift map. Homoclinic phenomena.

MATH 541.name: Manifold Theory
MATH 541.description: Differentiable manifolds, smooth mappings, tangent cotangent bundles, differential of a map, submanifolds, immersions, imbeddings, vector fields, tensor fields, differential forms, orientation on manifolds, integration on manifolds, Stokes' theorem. Lie derivative of tensor fields.

MATH 543.name: Methods of Applied Mathematics I
MATH 543.description: Functions spaces, orthogonal polynomials and Fourier analysis, generalized functions. Ordinary differential equations, Green's function, Sturm-Liouville problem, hypergeometric functions. Perturbation methods, regular perturbations, singular perturbations, boundary layer analysis, the WKB approximation.

MATH 544.name: Methods of Applied Mathematics II
MATH 544.description: Calculus of variations, necessary conditions for extrema, isoperimetric problems. Partial differential equations. Cauchy Kowalevsky theorem, linear, quasi-linear, half-linear equations. Initial and boundary value problem for the wave and heat equations, Riemann method. Laplace equation, minimum and maximum principles. Integral transforms. Stability and bifurcation. Inverse scattering transform.

MATH 550.name: Probability and Statistics
MATH 550.description: Mathematical foundations of Probability theory. Random walk. Consequence of probability measures. Sequences and sums of independent random variables. Markov chains. Percolation theory.

MATH 551.name: Topics in Number Theory
MATH 551.description: Local and global class field theory. p-adic analysis. Iwasawa theory. Modular forms. L-functions. Galois representations. Galois cohomology.

MATH 553.name: Ergodic Theory
MATH 553.description: Borel spaces. Borel automorphism. Poincare recurrence lemma. Ergodic theorem for permutations. Almost periodic functions. Birkhoff and Von neumann ergodic theorems. Return times. Applications to the number theory. Ergodic theorem for Markow chains. Ergodicity. Mixing. Irrational rotation. Diadic adding machine. Bernoulli, Markov, Kolmogorov shifts. Entropy.

MATH 564.name: Mathematical Foundations of Statistical Learning Theory
MATH 564.description: Statistical learning fundamentals. Concentration inequalities. Probably approximately correct learning framework. Empirical risk minimization, Vapnik-Chervonenkis theory, Rademacher averages. Binary classification. Regression with quadratic loss. Applications in signal processing, information theory, and control theory.

MATH 565.name: Mathematical Foundations of Data Science
MATH 565.description: Review of eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Fundamental subspaces, matrix factorization techniques, principal components and best low-rank matrices; the structure of neural nets for deep learning. Convergence concepts and limit theorems in probability, basic inequalities of probability, tail bounds, the concentration of measures phenomena, empirical process. Maximum likelihood estimation, regularized regression, the Lasso and its variations. Optimization methods, gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, convolutional neural nets.

MATH 573.name: Introduction to Financial Mathematics
MATH 573.description: Basic knowledge and techniques in financial mathematics: basic Black and Scholes model and its sophistications. Theory of discrete and continuous martingales, semimartingales. Stochastic integral, Ito formula, construction and solution of stochastic differential equations. Applications to option pricing and hedging problems for the European options. American options and the numerical problems of the solutions of second order elliptic equations.

MATH 574.name: Financial Mathematics
MATH 574.description: Calculations practiced in option marketing. Fundamentals of Itô Calculus, and its applications to calculations.

MATH 584.name: Topics in Mathematical Physics II
MATH 584.description: Spacetime geometry (curvature tensors, Cartan's equations, Bianchi identities, Gauss-Codazzi equations), action principles (Einstein-Hilbert action, ADM formalism), geodesic congruences (Raychaudhuri Eq, energy conditions), junction conditions.

MATH 585.name: Topics in Ordinary Differential Equations I

MATH 586.name: Topics in Ordinary Differential Equations II

MATH 597.name: Graduate Seminars in Mathematics I
MATH 597.description: Each graduate student who enrolls must present at least one one-hour talk about his/her research topic. Attendance to the seminars is mandatory.

MATH 598.name: Graduate Seminars in Mathematics II
MATH 598.description: Each graduate student who enrolls must present at least one one-hour talk about his/her research topic. Attendance to the seminars is mandatory.

MATH 599.name: Master's Thesis
MATH 599.description: A research-based thesis course that offers students the opportunity to work on a comprehensive, individual project. Topic to be agreed in consultation with a supervisor. The project will be of suitable complexity for results to be presented for an expert audience.

MATH 601.name: Topics in Real Analysis
MATH 601.description: Polynomial interpolation, Lebesgue functions and Lebesgue constants. Hermite interpolation and Birkhoff interpolation. Uniform approximation of functions. Approximation by integral operators. Characterization of best approximations. Haar systems. Degree of approximation, Jackson and Bernstein theorems. Polynomial inequalities. Classical orthogonal polynomials. Interpolation and approximation by splines.

MATH 609.name: Several Complex Variables
MATH 609.description: General theory: Holomorphic functions of several complex variables, integral formulas, Bergman kernel, domains of holomorphy, holomorphic convexity, plurisubharmonicity, d-bar problem. Special theory: Function theory on the unit ball, automorphisms, Hardy spaces, boundary behavior.

MATH 611.name: Algebraic Topology I
MATH 611.description: Categories and functors, homotopy of paths, homotopy of maps, fundamental groups, higher homotopy groups, homology of complexes, chain homotopy, standard simplices, the singular complex, singular homology, excision theorem, Mayer-Vietoris sequences, applications of homology.

MATH 612.name: Fibre Bundles I
MATH 612.description: A review of homotopy theory; obstruction theory. Vector bundles as a special case of Steenrod bundles; the principal bundle and associated fibrations. Characteristic classes as first obstructions; basic properties, Cartan's formula. The rings of characteristic classes. The splitting principle and further properties. Characteristic classes and manifolds; applications to cobordisms (Thom's theorem). An introduction to Schubert calculus. The topological Riemann-Roch theorem.

MATH 616.name: Topics in Group Theory
MATH 616.description: Finite p-groups and extremal families. Coxeter groups. Fitting subgroup. Groups of Lie type and BN pairs. Local group theory. Overview of classification of simple finite groups.

MATH 624.name: Compact Lie Groups
MATH 624.description: Compact Lie groups. Classical examples. One parametric subgroups. Maximal tori. Invariant differential operators and Lie algebras. Relation between Lie groups and algebras. Killing invariant form. Universal enveloping algebra. Cartan subalgebras. Roots systems. Weyl group. Dynkin diagrams and classification of roots systems. Exceptional Lie groups and algebras.

MATH 625.name: Homological Algebra
MATH 625.description: The course starts with standard material on homological algebra and continues with a special interest topic with instructor's consent such as special applications and calculations in algebraic topology, algebraic geometry or cohomology of groups. The standard part includes material on modules, categories, extensions of modules, derived functors and spectral sequences.

MATH 626.name: Cohomology of Groups
MATH 626.description: Group extensions. Basic homological algebra. Definition and properties of group cohomology. Serre's theorem. Mislin's theorem. Quillen's stratification theorem. Even's norm map and Steenrod operations. HLS - spectral sequence. Group actions on cell complexes

MATH 630.name: Commutative Algebra
MATH 630.description: Fundamental operations on monomial ideals, primary decomposition and associated primes, square free monomial ideals and simplicial complexes, The Alexander Dual, Monomial orders and Grobner bases, initial terms with respect to weights, generic initial ideals, Borel-fixed ideals, extremal Betti numbers.

MATH 631.name: Topics in Commutative Algebra
MATH 631.description: Basic notions of homological algebra. Graded free resolutions and syzygies. Kozsul complexes, pure and linear resolutions. Hilbert functions. Some selected topics like lex ideals, multicompression and Gotzmann's Persistence theorems.

MATH 632.name: Computational Commutative Algebra
MATH 632.description: Grobner bases, applications to operations on ideals, zero dimensional ideals, local monomial orders and ideals of leading forms, Grobner bases for modules, Grobner bases of toric ideals, applications to some other classes of ideals that appear in combinatorial commutative algebra.

MATH 633.name: Algebraic Geometry I
MATH 633.description: Transcendental theory; Complex algebraic varieties, line bundles and divisors, Riemann surfaces as algebraic curves, Hurwitz's theorem, Riemann-Roch theorem, uniformization, surfaces, Kodaira dimension, main classification theory of surfaces via birational theory, Chern classes, fixed point theorems, residues, spectral sequences.

MATH 645.name: Riemannian Geometry I
MATH 645.description: Smooth Manifolds, Riemannian Metrics and Levi-Civita Connections. Covariant Differentiation of Vector Fields. Riemannian Manifolds. Curvature, Geodesics, Exponential Map, Normal Coordinates. Sectional, Ricci and Scalar Curvatures. Gradient, Divergence and Laplacian Operators. Riemannian Submanifolds, Induced Connection, Second Fundamental Form, Formulae of Gauss and Weingarten. Equations of Gauss, Codazzi and Ricci.

MATH 646.name: Riemannian Geometry II
MATH 646.description: The Gauss lemma, Riemannian distance, Riemannian completeness, Hopf-Rinow theorem. Jacobi fields, symmetric spaces, isometries and killing vector fields. First and second variations, the index form, conjugate and focal points, homogeneous spaces, lie groups and lie algebras. Complex and almost complex manifolds. Hermitian and Kaehlerian manifolds.

MATH 653.name: Introduction to Analytical Number Theory
MATH 653.description: Primes in an arithmetic progression; Gauss' sum; primitive characters; Dirichlet's class number formula; the distribution of the primes; Riemann's zeta-function and Dirichlet $L$-functions; Explicit formulae and prime number theorems; the large sieve and Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem.

MATH 654.name: Analytic Number Theory
MATH 654.description: Integer points, trigonometric sums, infinite products, entire functions, the gamma function, the Riemann zeta-function, zeros of the zeta-function, the prime number theorem, Drichlet $L$-functions, primes in arithmetic progressions, the circle method, the Goldbach conjecture, Waring's problem.

MATH 699.name: Ph.D. Dissertation
MATH 699.description: A research-based thesis course that offers students the opportunity to work on a comprehensive, individual project. Topic to be agreed in consultation with a supervisor. The project should produce original research suitable for publication in a reputable scholarly journal.
